Standard input begins with a line containing an integer m, the number of fields in the schema. Each of the next m lines describes one field, in the order fields must be checked, as five space-separated tokens:
  name type required min max
where type is one of int, float, string or bool; required is yes or no; and min/max are either numbers (for int/float, bounds on the value; for string, bounds on its length) or the character - meaning no bound. bool fields never have bounds (min and max will always be - for them).

Check the fields in the exact order they appear in the schema. For each field, in this order, check: (1) is it required and missing from the document -- if so the error is "missing: <name>"; (2) if present, does its value fail to parse as the declared type (int must be a valid integer, float a valid decimal number, bool exactly "true" or "false", string always parses) -- if so the error is "type: <name>"; (3) if it parses, does the parsed value (or, for string, its length) fall outside the given min/max bounds -- if so the error is "range: <name>". As soon as a field fails one of these checks, stop and print that single error message and nothing else.

If every field in the schema passes all of its checks, print the single word "valid".

Example:
Input:
3
name string yes 1 20
age int yes 0 150
score float no - -
2
name=Alice
age=200
Output:
range: age

- LOWER: convert every line to lowercase

- COUNT: replace the entire set of lines with a single line containing the number of lines currently present

Example:

5
apple
banana
Apple
cherry
banana
3
LOWER
UNIQUE
SORT

apple
banana
cherry
